answer.summary: For a fixed linear regression model with an intercept and 3 predictors testing R-squared against zero at α = 0.05, with N = 80 participants and anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, the noncentral F-test power is 0.5991 (approximately 59.9%).
answer.method: Noncentral F-distribution for multiple regression. Power computed as P(F > F_crit | λ) where F_crit is the critical value at significance level α from the central F-distribution with df₁ = 3 (number of predictors) and df₂ = 76 (N − p − 1), and λ = R² × (N − p − 1) / (1 − R²) is the noncentrality parameter derived from the anticipated R² = ρ² = 0.09.
assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors (p = 3)
Alternative hypothesis H₁: population R² > 0 (one-sided test)
Anticipated multiple correlation coefficient ρ = 0.30 (effect size)
Standard regression assumptions apply (linearity, homoscedasticity, normality of errors, independence)
Noncentrality parameter λ ≈ 7.517 derived from R² and sample size
limitations: Power calculation assumes the anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 is correct; actual power will differ if the true effect is smaller or larger
No attrition accounted for in the sample size; the actual analytic sample should match N = 80
Calculation does not account for missing data or multicollinearity, which could affect the effective degrees of freedom
The critical F-value (2.7249) assumes two-sided test structure with lower.tail = FALSE, appropriate for testing non-null R²

executions.code:
# Power calculation for F-test in multiple regression
# H0: R^2 = 0 vs H1: R^2 > 0

# Design parameters
N <- 80                    # Number of participants
p <- 3                     # Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
rho <- 0.30                # Anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level
df_numerator <- p          # Degrees of freedom for predictors
df_denominator <- N - p - 1  # Degrees of freedom for residuals

# Calculate R-squared from multiple correlation
R_squared <- rho^2

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# λ = R² × (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
lambda <- R_squared * df_denominator / (1 - R_squared)

# Critical F-value at alpha level
F_crit <- qf(alpha, df_numerator, df_denominator, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Power = P(F > F_crit | λ)
# This is computed from the noncentral F-distribution with noncentrality λ
power <- pf(F_crit, df_numerator, df_denominator, 
            ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Compile results
cat("Linear Regression Power Calculation\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of participants: %d\n", N))
cat(sprintf("Number of predictors: %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom (numerator): %d\n", df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom (denominator): %d\n", df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ): %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Anticipated R-squared: %.4f\n", R_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Critical F-value: %.4f\n", F_crit))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting
results_list <- list(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(results_list)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
